channel.title: Daily Science Intake
channel.description: We will include a daily research summary — from an AI creator — to listen to whenever, and use it as a way to increase our exposure to science! In a nutshell, lazy people's way of reading papers.
channel.itunes:author: Paz Nativ

item.title: From Fish to Quantum Computers: The Surprising Versatility of Selective Ion Exchange
item.description: Three papers trace the evolution of zinc-hexacyanoferrate materials from removing ammonia in seafood shipping containers to extracting high-purity rubidium from industrial waste. Together they reveal how targeted selectivity in ion exchange can unlock both niche applications and critical materials recovery from complex brines.

item.title: When pH Lies: The Hidden Chemistry of Hypersaline Brines
item.description: pH is supposed to tell us if water is acidic or corrosive — but in super salty brines from lithium mines and oil wells, pH readings can be dangerously misleading. Researchers analyzed over 60,000 hypersaline water samples and found that more than 5% had acidic pH values yet weren't corrosive at all. We explore why standard measurements break down in extreme environments and what it means for environmental regulations and industrial processes.

item.description: In this episode, Paz dives into the remarkable discovery that water may exist as two distinct liquids at low temperatures. A mind-bending look at the most familiar yet mysterious substance on Earth.
